summary: SSE stream cuts final whitespace and punctuation after HTTP/2 priority preemption behind customer's edge proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that SSE streams delivered to their web clients occasionally arrive with the final characters (trailing whitespace and punctuation) missing. The content is syntactically complete but the last sentence sometimes loses a trailing space or final period, which breaks downstream client-side heuristics that expect a newline/terminator.

Impact:
- Affects BrightDocs' production readers in us-east (enterprise account).
- Visible as malformed final paragraphs in ~0.2% of long streaming responses for a subset of sessions; higher during bursts.
- Customer considers this a data-integrity issue for document export pipelines and flagged it as high priority.

Environment:
- Customer located behind an enterprise edge proxy that uses HTTP/2 with priority and stream preemption enabled.
- Requests from browser -> edge proxy (h2) -> Redwood API Gateway (h1/h2) -> serving runtime.
- Observed on models: gpt-large-v2, redwood-compat-1.0.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Client opens SSE connection to /v1/stream with long completion (>512 tokens) over HTTP/2 through their edge proxy.
2) Under simulated burst (20 concurrent streams from same client IP) the client sees the SSE session finish normally but the last token is missing trailing whitespace/punctuation in ~1/500 sessions.
3) Replaying the same request bypassing the edge proxy (direct to Redwood) does not reproduce.

Logs / evidence provided by customer (sanitized):
- Edge proxy debug: "PRIORITY_UPDATE stream=124 preempted-by=86" followed by "STREAM_HALF_CLOSED" at the same timestamp.
- Client observations: final SSE data event contained valid JSON but missing final space and ".".
- Server access log: upstream 200 OK and Content-Length reported matches payload; socket close shows short write on last segment.
- Customer captured wireshark/pcap that shows small 0-length data frame sequence around stream termination coincident with priority frames.

Requested outcome:
- Prevent loss of final characters so downstream tools consuming SSE do not get malformed last tokens.
- Understand whether this is a customer edge proxy bug, a compatibility issue with our gateway, or an intermediary interaction that needs mitigation in the platform.
comments: 2026-03-12 11:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Assigned to SRE for triage. Requested pcap and edge proxy config from customer. First response: asked for sample request id and timestamps.

2026-03-12 14:30 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Initial triage — reproduced a very similar symptom in our internal lab by enabling HTTP/2 priority preemption on an nginx-based proxy and streaming a long response. Observed truncated final whitespace in ~1/1000 runs. Filed hypothesis that priority reordering can steal the final chunk if socket-level write coalescing occurs at the proxy boundary.

2026-03-12 16:05 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Collected traces: linked span IDs to trace in observability: https://obs.redwood.ai/trace/abc123 (sensitive view). Upstream responded with full body and normal end-of-stream; the proxy sent a PRIORITY_UPDATE and then a half-close before flush completed.

2026-03-13 09:18 - Dev (Evan Chen): Reviewed reproduction notes. Hypothesis: our gateway writes final SSE delimiter as a very small write ("\n\n") and some HTTP/2 proxies with aggressive priority handling or write coalescing may drop trailing bytes when a stream is preempted or RST_STREAM races with end-of-stream. Proposed temporary mitigation: coalesce final delimiter into same buffer as last token to ensure single write syscall at gateway.

2026-03-13 11:46 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Tested Dev's coalescing patch in staging (serving-runtime PR #1820). Results: no occurrences in 50k long-stream requests behind nginx-priority emulation. Pushed patch to canary for customer-specific route.

2026-03-14 08:05 - BrightDocs support contact (Helen Zhou): Confirmed that after canary route applied they no longer see trimmed final characters in the last 48 hours in their smoke tests. Planning to disable priority on their edge proxy as an extra precaution while platform mitigation rolls out cluster-wide.

2026-03-14 10:12 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Next steps — schedule global rollout of coalescing fix, add observability metric to detect SSE-final-byte-loss (heuristic comparing last-token checksums), and create KB article recommending websocket fallback or proxy priority disable while using SSE for very long streams.

2026-03-14 12:00 - Evan Chen (Dev): Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1820 (coalesce final SSE delimiter into last write) and added unit test covering http2-proxy preemption path.
2026-03-14 12:22 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer notified of canary success and given recommended mitigations. Keeping ticket open until patch is rolled out and automated detection is in place.
resolution: Workaround applied: coalescing final SSE delimiter into last write (canary) + customer disabled HTTP/2 priority on their proxy. Temporary mitigation confirmed by customer. Long-term: global rollout of coalescing fix and add detection metric. Follow-up task INT-800901 created for rollout automation.
workaround: 1) Customer disabled HTTP/2 priority on their edge proxy for routes to Redwood OR 2) Use websocket streaming fallback for sessions that must preserve trailing whitespace until the global fix is rolled out.
